question_text: Find the perimeter and area of triangle ABC:

mark_breakdown.desc: Use trigonometric ratios to find side lengths $AB$ and $BC$
Calculate perimeter accurately to 3 significant figures
Calculate triangle area accurately to 3 significant figures

subparts.solution:
$\sin 41^\circ = \frac{7}{AB} \implies AB = \frac{7}{\sin 41^\circ}$
$\tan 41^\circ = \frac{7}{BC} \implies BC = \frac{7}{\tan 41^\circ}$

$\text{Perimeter} = AB + BC + AC$
$= \frac{7}{\sin 41^\circ} + \frac{7}{\tan 41^\circ} + 7$
$\approx 25.7\text{ cm}$

$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times AC \times BC$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times 7 \times \frac{7}{\tan 41^\circ}$
$\approx 28.2\text{ cm}^2$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: In a right-angled triangle, $\sin\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$ and $\tan\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$. The area is $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.
step_by_step: Identify opposite side $AC = 7\text{ cm}$ relative to the angle $41^\circ$.
Add all three side lengths to find the perimeter.
Use the formula $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times AC \times BC$ to calculate the area.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Mixing up opposite and adjacent sides relative to angle $B = 41^\circ$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Find lengths of $AB$ and $BC$ using trigonometry in $\triangle ABC$
Obtain perimeter $\approx 24.0\text{ m}$ and area $\approx 21.5\text{ m}^2$

subparts.solution:
$\hat{ABC} = 90^\circ - 28^\circ = 62^\circ$ {angles in triangle BCD}

Now in triangle ABC:
$\tan 62^\circ = \frac{9}{BC} \implies BC = \frac{9}{\tan 62^\circ}$
$\sin 62^\circ = \frac{9}{AB} \implies AB = \frac{9}{\sin 62^\circ}$

$\text{Perimeter} = AB + BC + AC$
$= \frac{9}{\sin 62^\circ} + \frac{9}{\tan 62^\circ} + 9$
$\approx 24.0\text{ m}$

$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times AC \times BC$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times \frac{9}{\tan 62^\circ}$
$\approx 21.5\text{ m}^2$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: First deduce the unknown acute angle in the main right-angled triangle by angle subtraction in the sub-triangle, then apply standard right-triangle trigonometry.
step_by_step: In right triangle $ABC$ with opposite side $AC = 9\text{ m}$, find $BC = \frac{9}{\tan 62^\circ}$ and $AB = \frac{9}{\sin 62^\circ}$.
Compute the perimeter as $AB + BC + AC \approx 24.0\text{ m}$.
Compute the area as $\frac{1}{2} \times AC \times BC \approx 21.5\text{ m}^2$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the wrong angle ($28^\circ$ instead of $62^\circ$) for the overall triangle $ABC$.
